You can save a search using the Saved Search feature. Basically, you use the Search Messages function (<Ctrl+Shift+F>) which has the option to "Save as Search Folder".

content:
What's supposed to happen during the account setup is that, using OAuth2 for authorization as (I believe) Yahoo requires, a web browser window should pop up and prompt you through entering your credentials and choosing whether or not to link to Yahoo's address book and calendar.

The only version of Ubuntu I have available is 26.04. I just added a Yahoo account to Thunderbird 160 and it all went as I described above. But I used to have the earlier version and did not have a problem with this. I would say that your Ubuntu is confused about how to deal with the authentication web page.

Some things that might help...

- Make sure cookies are enabled in Thunderbird (see <Settings | Privacy & Security | Web Content | Accept cookies from sites>.)

- Remove any existing cookies from Yahoo in Thunderbird (see <Settings | Privacy & Security | Web Content | Show Cookies button>.)

- Remove any existing Yahoo entries in Saved Passwords (see <Settings | Privacy & Security | Passwords | View Saved Passwords>.)

- Try changing the default web browser to something else temporarily. You can change it back after a successful authorization. Or, confirm to the OS that your current browser is truly the default.

Then restart Thunderbird and try setting up the account again. Hopefully the authorization will complete successfully. Please let us know how it goes.

content:
I don't know how you did this, because Thunderbird does its best to prevent you from doing it, but you somehow have managed to create an IMAP account using the POP server name and the IMAP port. I wouldn't have thought that would work, but I guess it depends on how they have their servers set up. Anyway, no wonder it's acting like an IMAP account for you... because that's what it is. The behavior you describe is normal for an IMAP account - when you move a message out of Inbox it is by definition removed from Inbox on the server.

Here are ionos.com's correct settings according to them:

https://www.ionos.com/help/email/general-topics/ionos-mail-server-details-for-imap-pop3-and-smtp/

Maybe it would be helpful for you to review this article about IMAP and POP3 servers and how they differ:

The difference between IMAP and POP3 https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/difference-between-imap-and-pop3

To remove an Imap account folder, I would always suggest you first unsubscribe from seeing it, so it's removed from the Thunderbird view. Then later, if really want to delete it for good. Access webmail account and delete it off server.

The folders in italics are what is called 'no-select' folders. They cannot contain emails themselves, but can contain folders that do contain emails. Sometimes people use them as top level header type folders.

I've been searching for a bug report: This one seems close. https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1997705

Please try: rename the ghost/greyed out and in italics folder by adding an X to Start of folder name and then renaming back by removing the X. Immediately, Exit Thunderbird and do restart of Thunderbird. Does it change the grey italic folder back to a normal folder? If yes, then unsubscribe from seeing it.
